changes: Added packages/graph, a private subpackage holding the story/evidence visualizer migrated from the standalone proof-or-stop-graph repo (31 files, engines.node >=22.5.0 for node:sqlite, assets/ gitignored as build output). Added packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts, a thin handler reaching that package through a runtime dynamic import. Registered the bare `graph` command across nine fail-closed surfaces including process-fact-levels.ts. Documented the migration in docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md and a CLAUDE.md section. Deleted packages/graph/src/shells/cli/main.ts as dead code.
usage: Run `proof-or-stop graph` to open the browser visualizer on port 8731, or `proof-or-stop graph --json` for machine-readable counts. Flags: --root=<dir> to inspect another repo, --port=<n>, --no-open to skip launching a browser, --json. The SQLite index is written under the user cache dir keyed by a sha256 of the repo root, never into the inspected worktree.
expectedOutcome: `proof-or-stop graph --json` prints the story/edge/index-row counts for this repository without writing anything into the worktree, and `proof-or-stop graph --help` documents the four flags.
actualTranscript: `node bin/proof-or-stop.js graph --json` -> stories=369 edges=426 indexRows=24007. `graph --help` -> "Interactive story + evidence graph for this repository (reads story state; writes its index cache outside the repo)" followed by the four documented flags. git status --porcelain unchanged across the run.
outcomeDiff: No difference. Counts are live values that drift as stories are written; the story/edge figures matched the documented 369/426 and index rows grew with ongoing story writes, which is expected for a read-only index over changing state.
limitations: packages/graph is marked private and is not published to npm. The vendored browser bundles are gitignored build output reproduced by `npm --prefix packages/graph run build`; each is an optionalDependency and the web shell feature-detects it, so a missing bundle degrades one feature rather than breaking the page. The handler reaches the package by runtime dynamic import permanently, not incidentally: node:sqlite requires Node >=22.5 and a static import would pull it into the always-evaluated module graph of every CLI command, breaking the whole CLI on Node 20 (verified on real Node v20.19.6). The resolved import path is --root-influenceable, which matches the trust model already accepted for verifier/serve.ts. verify-no-project-writes measures effect by hashing every path before and after a scan, so any concurrent writer in the worktree - including Claude Code activity-hook appends - can trip it; it is reliable only when run without a co-tenant.
pitfalls: Twelve real defects were found across roughly twelve independent host review rounds, in code that eleven in-session reviewer passes had already approved; six were in guards written to close the previous finding. The recurring class was guards that prove they ran without proving they hold - vacuous assertions, dead assertions placed after the exit decision, invalid controls, and stale dist reporting PASS. Check discriminating power by negative control before trusting any new guard. Process traps that cost the most time: (1) every commit moves materialHash and unbinds prior reviewer verdicts, so a fix-then-re-review cadence guarantees a loop - batch fixes, then re-review once; (2) review_inventory_begin freezes a cutoff, and any unrelated write while it is open resets all lanes - epoch RI-003 died to two dev-memory commits of mine; (3) never git add -A while a subagent is in flight, it sweeps their staged files into your commit under your authorship; (4) the gate-failure counter trips the convergence breaker at 2, and story_resume --ack is human-only by design; (5) the global lattice/proof-or-stop binary on this machine is a stale 0.3.257 install symlinked into a different worktree - always use node bin/proof-or-stop.js. Also: a reviewer reporting a cited artifact as missing may simply have searched the wrong scope - verify before filing against signed evidence.
